title: Kohn--Luttinger Superconductivity in Flat Chern Bands
authors: Nianlong Zou, Cheng Xu, Yafis Barlas, Yang Zhang
abstract: Recent observations of superconductivity near correlated topological phases in flat bands suggest a facile link between flat-band geometry and electron pairing. In this work, we reveal a geometry-driven Kohn--Luttinger mechanism in which Landau-level-like form factors align the attractive lobe of the RPA-screened Coulomb interaction with the form-factor peak, generating an anomalously strong attractive channel near local band extrema. Using the Skyrmion lattice model as a minimal realization, we show that for spin-unpolarized pairing the form-factor magnitude enforces an emergent momentum-space translational symmetry and selects an extended-$s$ instability concentrated at small Fermi pockets, while for spin-polarized pairing the form-factor phase drives chiral $p$- and $f$-wave order without invoking spin fluctuations. The band-extrema enhancement persists in higher Landau-level analogs and survives finite-temperature screening and Berezinskii--Kosterlitz--Thouless phase fluctuations. Our work establishes quantum geometry as a key organizing principle for unconventional pairing in flat Chern bands.
summary: This theoretical work reveals that superconductivity in flat Chern bands is governed by a novel 'geometry-driven' Kohn--Luttinger mechanism. By analyzing the alignment between the attractive Coulomb interaction and geometric form factors, the authors predict specific pairing symmetries (s-wave or chiral p/f-wave) depending on spin polarization. This establishes quantum geometry as a fundamental principle organizing unconventional superconductivity in topological materials.
main_problem: The work investigates the mechanism driving superconductivity near correlated topological phases, specifically focusing on a geometry-driven Kohn--Luttinger (KL) pairing mechanism.
main_result: They establish that quantum geometry dictates optimal pairing strength in flat Chern bands, leading to extended-$s$-wave instability for unpolarized pairing and chiral $p$/$f$-wave order for spin-polarized pairing.
method: The analysis uses the Random Phase Approximation (RPA) screening of the Coulomb interaction within the framework of a gap equation solved on the Skyrmion lattice model.
model_or_system: The system is modeled using flat Chern bands, realized minimally via the Skyrmion lattice model. The effective attraction is derived from RPA-screened interactions and analyzed near local band extrema.
key_observables: Superconducting transition temperature ($T_c$), order parameter ($\Delta$), pairing symmetry (s-wave, p-wave, f-wave), and superfluid stiffness ($D(T)$).
important_parameters:
Fermi filling ($
u$), magnetic length scale ($l_B$), and the degree of spin polarization.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on approximating the form factor near band extrema and uses the Skyrmion lattice model as a minimal realization for flat Chern bands.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the band structure, comparison between SLM and LLL form factors, RPA potential strength vs. filling, and $T_c$ dependence on filling and temperature effects.
paper_structure: The paper first introduces the geometry-driven KL mechanism using the Skyrmion lattice model Hamiltonian and RPA screening. It then analyzes spin-unpolarized and spin-polarized pairing channels separately to determine the resulting superconducting symmetry and stability, concluding with finite-temperature analysis.
why_interesting: While focused on superconductivity, the concept of geometric constraints (quantum geometry) dictating emergent many-body phases is highly relevant to understanding topological order in synthetic quantum platforms or engineered lattice systems studied in AMO physics.
